memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Please let us pass through your country. We will not go through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will travel along the King's Highway and not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory." But Edom answered: "You may not pass through here; if you try, we will march out and attack you with the sword." — Num 20:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses' request could hardly have been more reasonable. Israel promises not to touch Edom's fields or vineyards, not even to drink from their wells, but simply to pass through on the main road. Yet Edom's answer is a flat, hostile refusal, backed by a threat of the sword. Israel had done everything right, and still they were turned away.

This is a hard reality of life: sometimes we do everything right and are still refused, rejected, or opposed. Moses had been courteous, honest, and humble, asking for something small. Edom's harsh response was not deserved. When we have genuinely sought peace and are met with hostility anyway, it can be deeply discouraging.

But notice what Israel does not do. They do not force their way through in retaliation. Even facing an unjust refusal, they do not take matters violently into their own hands. There is a quiet strength in restraint, in not repaying hostility with hostility even when we feel wronged. Sometimes faithfulness means accepting a closed door rather than kicking it down.

We can trust God even when others shut doors in our faces. A refusal from people is not the end of God's plan. He can lead us by another way, as He would lead Israel around Edom. When you have done all you can to seek peace and are still rejected, do not let bitterness take root. Entrust the injustice to God, who judges rightly, and follow the example of Christ, who, when reviled, did not retaliate but trusted His Father. God's purposes are not thwarted by the closed doors of others.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you experienced doing everything right and still being refused?
2. Why is there strength in restraint when we are unjustly opposed?
3. How can you entrust rejection and injustice to God rather than growing bitter?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I have sought peace and am met with rejection, guard my heart from bitterness and retaliation. Help me to trust that Your purposes are not thwarted by closed doors. Give me the restraint and trust that Christ showed. Amen.
